title: orcad: an environment switch that keeps the browser provider from launching an installed Orca desktop app
problem: A host process that runs orcad headless as a child service may supply its own browser, or may run on a machine where the user also has the Orca desktop app installed. orcad's browser provider looks for an installed Orca desktop executable at its fixed install paths and, when it finds one, launches it as a hidden Electron browser. The embedding host has no way to turn that off, so orcad starts a second, invisible copy of the desktop app that the host did not ask for and cannot account for.
change: installedElectronCandidates returns an empty list when ORCA_DISABLE_INSTALLED_ELECTRON_BROWSER is '1'. With no candidate, resolveOrcadBrowserProvider falls through to ORCA_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE, or reports that no provider is configured, exactly as it already does on a machine without the desktop app. The switch is unset by default, so stock behaviour is unchanged.
testing: New file src/main/orcad/orcad-browser-provider.installed-electron-switch.test.ts. With the switch unset, or set to any value other than '1', the installed-Electron candidate list on macOS, Linux and Windows equals the list without the variable. With the switch set to '1' the list is empty on all three platforms, and resolveInstalledElectronExecutable given that list resolves nothing.
